亞茲琴為古代泰米爾音樂使用的弦鳴樂器，至少公元前二世紀印度已有拱形豎琴傳統，巴魯: The yazh is a chordophone used in ancient Tamil music. India had an arched-harp tradition at least by the second century BC, and a Buddhist carving at Bhārut shows a woman holding the instrument. From about the seventh century, as the stick-zither vina rose, the Indian harp-vina and the yazh declined. Its form and name appear in Sangam literature, in the Tirukkural and in the Silappatikaram, the last of which records four types; temple carvings and religious texts also preserve the occasions on which it was played. Modern and contemporary makers have reconstructed it from works of art, and Sri Lankan Tamil legend and place names also reflect its spread.
亞茲琴的琴身以本地木材鑿製，來源提到紅木與菠蘿蜜木，現代則用紅雪松。共鳴箱呈船形: The body of the yazh is carved from local timber; the source mentions rosewood and jackwood, and modern instruments use red cedar. The soundbox is boat-shaped or trough-shaped, and its opening is covered with goatskin as a soundboard, glued with a paste made from tamarind seeds. The strings are gut, running from the curved ebony neck to the soundbox; the neck may also be covered with hide. The string post or tuning post below the soundboard is fixed to the body with arakku lac, and the strings pass through the soundboard and are tied to it.
亞茲琴音色溫潤深沉，具有古典蒼涼的韻味。由於採用腸弦製作，琴弦振動產生的音質柔和: The yazh has a warm, deep timbre with a classical, desolate flavour. Because the strings are gut, the tone they produce is soft and fine-grained, with clear layers of overtones. Its range is wide, running from a low, full bass to a clear, transparent treble, and it is expressive. The skin soundboard and the boat-shaped soundbox give the instrument a resonance of its own; it is neither as bright and clear as the harp nor as strongly metallic as the pipa, but offers an old-fashioned, inward-looking Eastern tone. The sound carries well, and in ancient Tamil music it showed a particular expressiveness and emotional tension; it suits pieces that are meditative and contemplative.
亞茲琴（泰米爾語：யாழ்，也音譯為 yāḻ，發音為 [jaːɻ]）是古代泰米爾: The yazh (Tamil: யாழ், also transliterated yāḻ, pronounced [jaːɻ]) is a harp used in ancient Tamil music. Its strings are gut, running from a curved ebony neck to a boat-shaped or trough-shaped soundbox whose opening is covered with a skin soundboard. At the soundbox the strings are attached to a string bar or tuning bar pierced with holes for the strings, set below the soundboard and projecting through it. The neck may also be covered with hide.
坐姿將琴靠於肩上或置於身前。將樂器穩定持於身前。左手負責按弦或改變有效弦長以控制: Play seated, resting the instrument against the shoulder or holding it in front of the body. Hold the instrument steady in front of you. The left hand stops the strings, or changes their sounding length, to control pitch, and the right hand sets the strings vibrating. A chordophone sounds by way of the strings' vibration amplified by the soundbox. Pluck the strings with the fingertips or a plectrum, paying attention to the angle and the force of contact.
